$$
{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt[3]{y}-2}^{y}{\int }_{y/2}^{x+4}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y={\int }_{-3}^{p}{\int }_{-1}^{q}{\int }_{y/2}^{x+4}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{r}^{1}{\int }_{y/2}^{x+4}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Changing the Order of Integration in Triple Integrals: Changing Projection

examples.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration When the Projection Is Partitioned
examples.problem:
By changing the order of integration in the following repeated integrals so that they are integrated first with respect to $z,$ then $y,$ and then $x,$ express the following sum as a single repeated integral.

$$
\displaystyle
\int_{-1}^0 \int_{y^2}^{1} \int_{x-1}^{y^2} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y
+
\int_0^1 \int_{y}^{1} \int_{x-1}^{y^2} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y
$$
examples.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
\int_a^b \int_{v_1(x)}^{v_2(x)} \int_{u_1(x,y)}^{u_2(x,y)}  f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x.
$$

From the repeated integrals, we see that the domain of integration $R = R_1\cup R_2,$ where $R_1$ and $R_2$ are type I regions, is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & ={(x,y,z)\,:\,-1\le y\le 0,\,\,{y}^{2}\le x\le 1,\,\,x-1\le z\le {y}^{2}}, \\ {R}_{2} & ={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,y\le x\le 1,\,\,x-1\le z\le {y}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
\int_a^b \int_{v_1(x)}^{v_2(x)} \int_{x-1}^{y^2} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/c8bfd933472e1944f63b1295bda7fc324311ea2ca2ada3636e9f5ab82e4e5fc5.png)

The region $D$ consists of two type II regions in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D =
\left\{ (x,y) \: : \: -1 \leq y \leq 0, \quad y^2 \leq x \leq 1 \right\}
\:\cup\:
\left\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \quad y \leq x \leq 1 \right\}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y$ to $\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the lower boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
x=y^2
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
y = -\sqrt{x}
$$

and the upper boundary of the region is

$$
x=y
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
y =x.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region is

$$
D = \left\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \quad -\sqrt{x} \leq y \leq  x \right\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/c73a0e30d6996490f9f41bf3e8777c14d542755387f643ad464bd1dd6cab2839.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\int_0^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{1}} \int_{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{-\sqrt{x}}}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{x}} \int_{x-1}^{y^2} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x.
$$

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/fcc776a63cd1ac9fc5ec91157652ce9e75c6ee515eca8c6223309521cc300b61.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{1}^{4}{\int }_{-4/x}^{-1}{\int }_{0}^{2+xy/2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $x,$ and then $y.$
feedback.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,1\le x\le 4,\,\,-\frac{4}{x}\le y\le -1,\,\,0\le z\le 2+\frac{xy}{2}}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{0}^{2+xy/2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/1f30c28c7c048faae864da08a5a6d67d0c6346b27c00a9e7726234531f2f0783.png)

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 4,\,\,-\frac{4}{x}\le y\le -1}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the right boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is 

$$
y=-\frac{4}{x}\,⟹\,x=-\frac{4}{y}
$$

and the left boundary of the region is

$$
x=1.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-4\le y\le -1,\,\,1\le x\le -\frac{4}{y}},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/acc210f36bccb873526172149b85941bd42bc1648a464862562723fedca27bcb.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{-4}^{-1}{\int }_{1}^{-4/y}{\int }_{0}^{2+xy/2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.
$$
